title: What Exactly Happens to Your Soul After You Die? - Monday: Maamar Yafeh Sha'ah Achas #8
blurb: The Pain of Saying Goodbye to Fakeness: When All Illusions Disappear and You Encounter Who You Really Are What really happens to us after we die? What are Gan Eden and Gehenna? Are heaven and hell two different destinations, or two radically different experiences of the same reality? In this extraordinary class, exploring the profound teachings of the Mitteler Rebbe, Rabbi YY Jacobson takes us on a remarkable journey into the soul's experience after death, describing what unfolds when the body falls away and the soul encounters the unfiltered truth of its existence. Every thought, word, desire, craving, action, and experience generates spiritual energy that never disappears. After death, the soul encounters the reality it has created, without the protective veil of denial. Heaven and hell are not merely external rewards and punishments; they are the soul's experience of its own accumulated reality. The soul, which is inherently Divine and infinite, longs to dissolve into its Source. But if a lifetime has been invested in constructing an identity of separateness, insecurity, ego, and falsehood, surrendering that identity can feel unbearable. What is paradise for one soul may become excruciating torment for another. Yet the most transformative revelation is that this process does not begin after death. title: Samach Vav Part 252: Kabolas ol regulates the ratzo; it is decidedly b'koach atzmo
blurb: Samach Vav p. 203-204: Hanochos atzmuso of kabolas ol also regulates the ratzo so that it (not become overly excited and intense, but) be followed by integration of shuv. For example: The joy of the king's minister attending a celebratory feast of the king is tempered by his reverence for the king (unlike a close advisor of the king, whose joy is revealed and reverence concealed), like a servant whose constant dedication to his master never lets him cross the line into defiance, even when he is joyous. This kabolas ol is decidedly self-generated by the person (m'koach atzmo), not due to an inspiration from above, but through his choice and volition (bechira v'ratzon) to accept and crown G-d as his sovereign King. Nevertheless, we must say that this kabolas ol is due to the core soul being bound and united with Atzmus. However, this bond is very concealed, to the point that the essential kabolas ol is b'koach atzmo.
